REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2, u3, uF
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u3
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, blocker_moved & has_door_key) -> u1
(u0, key_lost) -> uF
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, door_open) -> u2
(u1, key_lost) -> uF
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, target_picked_up) -> u3
(u2, key_lost) -> uF
(u2, else) -> u2
(u3, else) -> u3
(uF, else) -> uF
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, blocker_moved & has_door_key, u1) -> 0.1
(u1, door_open, u2) -> 0.3
(u2, target_picked_up, u3) -> 1.0
(u0, key_lost, uF) -> -0.5
(u1, key_lost, uF) -> -0.5
(u2, key_lost, uF) -> -0.5
feedback: Accepted. Semantic fidelity: the task 'Don't drop the key while the door is still closed' is exactly the key_lost event (has_door_key true at t-1, false at t, door_open false at t), and the RM handles it as an explicit one-step regression: key_lost sends u0/u1/u2 to the absorbing failure state uF with a single -0.5 penalty, after which all rewards are forfeited, so a violating trajectory can never out-earn a clean one. Success is grounded in u3 (target_picked_up), which is declared in STATES, listed in the nonempty FINAL_STATES header, and reachable via u0->u1->u2->u3. The progress chain is physically faithful: door_open cannot occur before blocker_moved and has_door_key (the ball's cell is the only toggle cell and the matching key is required), and target_picked_up cannot occur before door_open, so no completing trajectory is excluded or left unrewarded. The u0 conjunction is well-posed: blocker_moved & has_door_key first co-occur when the key is picked up after the ball has been moved and dropped elsewhere (carrying is exclusive), it is disjoint from key_lost (which requires has_door_key false), and disjoint from door_open timing issues only by one step (door_open persists, so u1->u2 fires the following step; if the door is shut again it can be reopened since the ball is away), keeping the transition function deterministic. Key-first play necessarily fires key_lost (the ball blocks the only toggle cell and hands are occupied, so the key must be dropped while the door is closed), so routing that path to uF is faithful to the task, not an artifact. Persistent/event distinctions are correct: the event key_lost triggers dedicated penalty transitions rather than a lingering condition, while conditions gate progress; the door_open regression (toggled shut) is re-covered by the key_lost transitions in u1/u2, and irrelevant events (blocker_moved regression, has_door_key loss with the door open, turns/moves/done) fall into the per-state else self-loops, including absorbing else-loops for u3 and uF. Reward safety: rewards are bounded (max +1.4, monotone 0.1/0.3/1.0), the penalty is a single bounded -0.5 with no repeated negative self-loops, and there are no rewarded cycles, so no exploitation is possible. Format matches the paper: REWARD_MACHINE/STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES/TRANSITION_FUNCTION/REWARD_FUNCTION headers, comma-separated declared states, nonempty FINAL_STATES, (state, label) -> state transitions with else complements in every state, and (state, label, state) -> reward entries exactly matching the nonzero transitions. No issues requiring rejection.

All five environment-declared propositions are present, no extras, no missing predicates. Syntax is valid executable Python one-liners with no imports, actions, or side effects; env and episode memory are only read. blocker_moved: the candidate scans the grid for the (single) door and checks the cell at (x-1, y) for a ball, which is exactly the documented ball start cell (dx-1, dy); the guard 'x > 0' is harmless since the door lies in the interior shared wall. A carried ball is absent from the grid, so pickup counts as moved, and dropping the ball back on that cell makes it false again — matching the condition reading. has_door_key and door_open are verbatim matches to the documented grid-scan expressions. target_picked_up matches the mission-string condition exactly (no fixed color assumed). key_lost correctly implements the event semantics: it reads the read-only previous valuation, requires previous has_door_key true, and inlines the exact has_door_key and door_open expressions negated (not K and not D), so it can never co-occur with has_door_key, door_open, or (given one-action steps) target_picked_up. The leading bool(...) guard on the previous-valuation dict is redundant but safe and does not alter truth values under the documented contract that a complete valuation exists (all-false at step 0, so key_lost is false there). All attribute accesses are guarded against None cells, so no runtime errors; all constraint orderings (blocker_moved before door_open, has_door_key before door_open, target_picked_up after door_open) are respected by the expressions themselves.
